::: {#def-graph .theorem}
## Network graph

An ordered pair $\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{N},\psi)$ with node set $\mathcal{N}$, whose elements represent observational units, and adjacency function $\psi$, which represents potential causal influence between observational units. The network is directed: the adjacency function assigns a nonnegative weight $\psi(i,j)$ to each ordered pair of distinct observational units, the weight of $j$’s influence on $i$, and $\psi(i,j)$ need not equal $\psi(j,i)$.

$$
\mathcal{G}=(\mathcal{N},\psi),\qquad \psi:\mathcal{N}\times\mathcal{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0},\qquad \psi(i,i)=0.
$$

$j$ influences $i$ if and only if $\psi(i,j)>0$.

The neighborhood of an observational unit $i\in\mathcal{N}$ is the set of units that influence it:

$$
\mathcal{N}_i=\{j\in\mathcal{N}:\psi(i,j)>0\}.
$$

The network weights $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_i$ of unit $i$ are the $i$th row of the adjacency matrix, the weights of every unit’s influence on $i$, with $n=|\mathcal{N}|$:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Psi}_i=[\psi(i,1),\dots,\psi(i,n)]^T.
$$

For a covariate $\mathbf{X}$, the neighbor values $\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i}$ are the entries of $\mathbf{X}$ belonging to the neighborhood of $i$, in the order of their indices:

$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i}=\big(X_j\big)_{j\in\mathcal{N}_i}.
$$

We reserve *network value* for a summary of the neighbor values (C.19).
:::
